Common questions, known issues on this car, and the beeps
the car did not confirm the new setting. Check it in the car.
The connection to the adapter was lost.
The adapter answers but the car does not. Switch the power ON (or READY).

Plug the OBD adapter into the socket under the steering wheel. Pair it in the phone\'s Bluetooth settings if it is a classic Bluetooth adapter (PIN usually 1234 or 0000), then tap Choose adapter. Switch the car\'s power ON (no need for READY). Unplug the adapter when you leave the car for days, since it draws power from the 12 V battery.
No drive battery data yet. Connect and switch the car\'s power ON.
The drive battery data could not be read.

Values from the battery computer (BMU). Charge level, capacity and pack voltage are documented by owners; the cell values are inferred and marked experimental. Health uses Mitsubishi\'s figure for a new battery: 38 Ah before model year 2017, 40 Ah from 2017.
At rest a healthy 12 V battery shows about 12.6 V or more. Run the 12 V test for a proper check.
Above 13.2 V: the car is charging the 12 V battery (READY or charging).
No live values yet. Connect the adapter and switch the car\'s power ON.
Tap a value for its source. Values marked “owners” come from owner research; “experimental” values may be wrong on this car.
Experimental: may be wrong on this car
Also reads the drive battery, charger, motors and other units directly (read-only, takes longer).
Connect the adapter and switch the car\'s power ON first.

This clears the engine and emission codes (OBD-II mode 04) and the engine warning lamp. It also resets the emission self-tests, so the car may not be ready for the inspection for a while, and it erases the stored snapshot of the fault. Note the codes first. Codes in the drive battery, charger and motor units are not cleared (deliberately). Switch the power ON but do not run the engine.
This is a Mitsubishi-specific code; Mitsubishi does not publish its exact meaning. A workshop with a Mitsubishi diagnostic tool (MUT-III) can read the details.
General guidance for this kind of fault, not a diagnosis of your car. Never open high-voltage parts (orange cables, drive battery, inverter, charger) yourself.
Code or word, e.g. P0A80 or catalyst
Guided checks you can do on the spot. The app tells you what to do, measures, and explains the result.
How do I make the engine run?

Limits marked as estimates in the app documentation have no published value for this car. Treat results as a guide, and do the driving parts only where it is safe; the app measures by itself, so keep your eyes on the road.
Writes all live values once per second to a spreadsheet file, for example during a drive or a charge.
Could not start recording (see the log).
The bytes after “61 01”, numbered from 00. Useful for decoding more values; share a screenshot with the project if you find something.
Sends commands straight to the adapter. Reading is harmless; only send commands you understand.
Adapters are listed first. Paired adapters are below; Scan finds Bluetooth LE adapters and classic ones that aren\'t paired yet.
The app needs permission to find and connect to nearby Bluetooth devices.
No paired adapters. Tap Scan below, or pair the adapter in the phone\'s Bluetooth settings.
Join the adapter\'s Wi-Fi network first (often “WiFi_OBDII” or “V-LINK”). The phone cannot use the car\'s own Wi-Fi at the same time.
The car\'s own customisable functions, changed over the car\'s Wi-Fi like in the official app. Tap a setting to change it; the car confirms and saves the change.
The car reports that its settings can\'t be changed right now (status %1$d).
Waiting for the car to send its settings…
Set all vehicle settings back to Mitsubishi\'s defaults?
Unnamed settings reported by the car

Your car reports these settings, but Mitsubishi\'s app never shows them and their effect is unknown. Note the current option before changing anything, and change it back if something behaves differently.
Lock/unlock beeps and horn answerback are in the “Keyless entry & operation” group. Tips → Beeps lists every sound and how to change it.
Collected from owner\'s manuals, recalls and owner communities, with sources. General advice, not a diagnosis of your car.
There is no volume setting for the warning sounds on this car, only on/off for some of them. Each sound below shows whether this app, the car\'s own menu or a switch, or only a dealer can change it.

“%1$s” is not a plain read request. Commands such as 04 (clear codes), 10 (session), 11 (reset), 14 (clear memory), 27 (security) or 2E/2F/31/3B (write/control) can change or reset the car\'s control units. Only continue if you know exactly what it does.
Tap “Read now” to fetch every cell voltage (car must be in READY or ignition ON).
Couldn\'t confirm the cell order against the pack summary — showing a best guess. Sharing the log (Settings → Diagnostics) helps pin the layout down.
Read the cells, but couldn’t confirm the layout — please share the diagnostics log.
Per-cell voltages from the battery ECU. Highlighted = highest and lowest cell.
